Russian prohibitions normally take the imperfective imperative («Не нарушай тишину в библиотеке»); the perfective negative imperative reads as a warning against accidental action, so a human should decide whether to reword or move the sentence to нарушать.

en_alt: Evening was coming on slowly.
Evening was slowly drawing in.
note: 'Drawing in' is the English idiom for days getting shorter, not for one evening arriving; 'evening was falling' is the standard rendering and keeps the imperfective progressive.

The sentence needs the temporal sense 'to set in / to come', which the headword gloss 'to advance' does not cover — three of this word's five examples render it that way, so the gloss may be the half that needs widening.

note: 'Spring will soon be advancing' applies the military sense of наступать to a season; the gloss 'to advance' is what pushed the sentence into nonsense.
